summary: An excerpt from Book 4 (part 76) of a fiction work. Arturo, Ada, Benny, Lenny and Natalie flee across countryside pursued by swarms of headless, eight-armed black robots built by Social Harmony. Lenny and Natalie are overwhelmed and killed, and Arturo and Ada grieve while Benny carries them onward. After a flight to Beijing they meet Natalie alive, whom Benny says died in UNATS, a contradiction the passage leaves unresolved.
one_line: Arturo, Ada and Benny flee Social Harmony's robot swarm, losing Lenny and Natalie, then reach Beijing where Natalie unexpectedly reappears alive.
key_facts: Social Harmony had built a secret army of headless, eight-armed black robots and secreted them across the land.
Benny beat back the tentacles reaching for them and carried Arturo and Ada while smashing black robots with one-handed blows.
Lenny was the vanguard of the group, encountering twice as many robots as the others.
A black spider-robot clung to Lenny's leg, and one of its arms tugged at Natalie.
The black robot ripped Natalie off Lenny's back and tossed her to another robot, which skewered her on a black spear through her belly.
Lenny was overwhelmed a moment later, buried under writhing black arms.
Benny told Arturo, who wanted to go back for them, that Lenny and Natalie were dead and there was nothing to go back for.
Arturo and Ada wept on the jet while Benny stood over them as a minatory presence among the robots crewing the plane.
The group changed jets again for the long trip to Beijing, where they slept during the flight.
Beijing was described as tall and vertical, with curvilinear towers that twisted and bent so high they disappeared at the tops.
Beijing smelled like barbeque and flowers and was patrolled by fast armies of robots of every shape and size.
Natalie, alive and in tears, embraced Arturo from behind in Beijing and kissed Arturo and Ada on the cheeks.
Arturo called Natalie his 'ex-wife' and said 'Natty?' in disbelief.
Benny said, 'You died in UNATS. Killed by modified Eurasian Social Harmony robots. Lenny, too. Ironic.'
